question.problem: Given the curve  $r(t)=(3t-1)\,i+2t\,j+\sqrt{3}t\,k,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=4t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
question.worked_solution:
First, since $s=4t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{4}.$  

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{4}) \\  & =(3\cdot \frac{s}{4}-1)i+(2\cdot \frac{s}{4})j+(\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac{s}{4})k \\  & =(\frac{3s-4}{4})i+\frac{s}{2}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}s}{4}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3s-4}{4})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{s}{2})j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{3}s}{4})k \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\,i+\frac{1}{2}\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$
